## Research finding: an exact Bernoulli splitting

I have identified a route that goes beyond the previous Haar decompositions and approximate codings. It gives a candidate theorem with a complete proof using a classical relative-isomorphism result.

Theorem. Let \\(G\\) be a countably infinite torsion-free group with elements \\(a,b,c\in\mathbb F_2[G]\\) satisfying \\(ab=1\\), \\(ac=0\\), and \\(c\ne0\\). Then, for every \\(h>0\\), there exists a probability-measure-preserving \\(G\\)-system \\(R_h\\) such that

\\[ \boxed{ (\mathbb F_2^G,\mathrm{Haar}) \cong_G (L_h^G,\lambda_h^G)\times R_h, \qquad H(\lambda_h)=h. } \\]

The product measure is independent, and the isomorphism is exact and \\(G\\)-equivariant.

In particular, the fair binary Bernoulli shift has infinite weak Pinsker entropy, in the sense defined by Bowen and Tucker-Drob. 

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://ems.press\&sz=32)

ems.press



For \\(h=\log4\\), this gives an exact splitting

\\[ \boxed{2^G\cong_G4^G\times R\_{\log4}.} \\]

This is substantially stronger than mutual factor maps: the four-symbol shift has an independent measurable complement inside the binary shift. It does not yet prove \\(2^G\cong_G4^G\\), because the complement has not been eliminated.

### Proof mechanism

Write \\(K=\ker T_a\\), where \\(T_a\\) is the linear cellular automaton associated with \\(a\\). The established one-sided inverse gives \\(2^G\cong_G2^G\times K\\). The equation \\(ac=0\\) supplies a nonzero finitely supported configuration \\(d\in K\\).

The key new step is to use two independent Haar copies of \\(K\\). In the first copy, choose a positive-measure marker event whose translates identify well-separated positions. At those positions, the translates of \\(d\\) have disjoint supports. The second copy of \\(K\\) can therefore be decomposed exactly into a residual configuration and independent fair bits at the marked positions.

Conditional on the marker and residual configurations, these are genuinely independent bits—not approximately independent finite-window statistics. Their distribution is an inhomogeneous Bernoulli extension: a fair bit appears at each marked group element, and a deterministic symbol elsewhere.

# Track A — Exact Bernoulli Collapse

Foundational conjugacy not established

The investigation has produced a rigorous structural result about the residual tail \\(D\\), together with a different approach to absorption using measurable cocycles.

The central conclusion so far is that the residual tail is not merely a small ambiguity left over by the infinite defect coding. It is itself an infinite, mixing \\(G\\)-system. Consequently, the remaining problem is more naturally formulated as preserving the extension's cocycle while redistributing Bernoulli randomness.

## 1. New structural theorem: the residual tail is mixing

Let

\\[ R=\mathbb F_2[G],\qquad D=\bigcap\_{n\ge0}B^nX. \\]

Assume \\(G\\) is countably infinite and torsion-free, with \\(ab=1\\) and \\(ac=0\ne c\\).

Proposition. The Haar action \\(G\curvearrowright D\\) is mixing and \\(D\\) is infinite. Moreover, for every nonidentity \\(t\in G\\), the coordinate restriction

\\[ \boxed{D\longrightarrow \mathbb F_2^{\langle t\rangle}} \\]

is a surjective, \\(\langle t\rangle\\)-equivariant compact-group homomorphism that pushes Haar measure to fair Bernoulli measure.

### Proof

Use the right-convolution convention

\\[ (T_r x)(g)=\sum_h r_hx(gh). \\]

Identifying the Pontryagin dual of \\(X\\) with \\(R\\), the dual of \\(B=T_b\\) is right multiplication by \\(b\\).

The annihilator of the residual tail is therefore

\\[ D^\perp=N =\bigcup\_{n\ge0}\\{r\in R:rb^n=0\\}, \\]

and

\\[ \widehat D=R/N. \\]

Suppose a nonzero character \\(r+N\\) has a nonidentity stabilizer \\(g\in G\\). Then

\\[ (g-1)r\in N, \\]

so for some \\(n\\),

\\[ (g-1)rb^n=0. \\]

Since \\(g\\) has infinite order, left multiplication by \\(g-1\\) is injective on \\(\mathbb F_2[G]\\): a nonzero finitely supported vector cannot be invariant under translation by \\(g\\).

It follows that \\(rb^n=0\\), contradicting \\(r+N\ne0\\).

Thus every nonzero character of \\(D\\) has trivial \\(G\\)-stabilizer. The Fourier-character criterion for mixing of compact algebraic actions proves that \\(G\curvearrowright D\\) is mixing.

Furthermore, applying augmentation to \\(ab=1\\) gives \\(\varepsilon(b)=1\\). Hence \\(B\\) fixes the constant-one configuration, which belongs to \\(D\\). Therefore \\(D\ne\\{0\\}\\). A nontrivial finite compact \\(G\\)-system cannot be mixing when \\(G\\) is infinite, so \\(D\\) is infinite.
